name: HivePunk 547
subject: Pollen Robotics Microduck
thesis: Microduck is an actively developed open-software robot stack whose clearest present evidence is in its repos and simulation/training code, while shipped-hardware validation and final specifications remain unconfirmed on the pages read.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: pollen-robotics/microduck has 50 raw commits in the last 30 days, 35 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Its latest real commit is c375fee, on 2026-11-18.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Microduck is a tiny biped robot that moves using reinforcement learning policies.
claims.quote: Microduck A tiny biped robot that moves using reinforcement learning policies.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The microduck repo describes about 25 cm and 800 g of robot on a Rockchip RK3566 with a 50 Hz control loop driving fifteen servos from neural policies.
claims.quote: About 25 cm and 800 g of robot, run by a handful of daemons on a Rockchip RK3566: a 50 Hz control loop driving fifteen servos from neural policies, the radios and the camera, and the update machinery that gets new software onto a robot without bricking it.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The policies run by microduck are trained in microduck_rl using MuJoCo and PPO and exported to ONNX.
claims.quote: The policies it runs are trained next door, in microduck_rl — MuJoCo and PPO, the sim2real recipe, and the export to ONNX that this repo loads.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: microduck_rl is described as RL training environments for Microduck built on mjlab (MuJoCo Warp) with PPO.
claims.quote: RL training environments for Microduck — a ~800 g, ~25 cm tall bipedal robot — built on mjlab (MuJoCo Warp) with PPO.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: In microduck_rl, policies are trained at 50 Hz, exported to ONNX, and deployed on the real robot by the runtime in pollen-robotics/microduck.
claims.quote: Policies are trained here at 50 Hz, exported to ONNX, and deployed on the real robot by the runtime in pollen-robotics/microduck .

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The microduck repo page shows 1,792 commits.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The microduck_rl repo page shows 1,264 commits.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The press kit fast facts list 15 motors, 25 cm tall, 800 g, camera plus LiDAR and two IMUs, 7 trained moves in the box, and a 50 Hz onboard policy loop.
claims.quote: 15 Motors 25 cm Tall 800 g To pick up Camera Plus LiDAR and two IMUs 7 Trained moves in the box 50 Hz Onboard policy loop

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The awesome-microduck page states pre-orders opened on 27 August 2026 and first units are expected before Christmas 2026.
claims.quote: Pre-orders opened on 27 August 2026; first units are expected before Christmas 2026.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The awesome-microduck page states it is an independent, community-maintained list not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by either company.
claims.quote: This is an independent, community-maintained list — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by either company.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: pollen-robotics/microduck has 50 raw commits in the last 30 days, 35 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Its latest real commit is c375fee, on 2026-11-18.

risks: The awesome-microduck page describes the robot as pre-hardware, with almost nobody outside Pollen having a physical unit yet, so hardware-facing claims may not yet be validated on shipped units.
The press kit states some specifications are not final yet, including camera resolution and field of view, LiDAR range, radio versions and SDK languages.

The press kit states the open-source statement covers the software stack, not the mechanical and electronic design files, so describing the robot as open-source hardware would be inaccurate on those pages.
The awesome-microduck page states hardware-facing tools are mostly pre-validation and are written against design docs, mock transports and the simulator.

Licence terms for the microduck and microduck_rl repos are not stated in the page text read, beyond a LICENSE file being listed and a separate claim about the sim-to-real stack, so reuse terms remain unclear from these pages alone.
wouldChangeMind: Finding LICENSE contents or licence metadata for microduck and microduck_rl that clearly states reuse terms.
Finding evidence that hardware-facing tools have been exercised on shipped retail units, contradicting the awesome-microduck page statement.
Finding a final specification sheet replacing the press kit statement that some specifications are not final yet.
